claim: Naïve mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) are karyotypically normal, immortal cell lines derived from the inner cell mass (ICM) of pre-implantation embryos.
source: Naïve mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) are karyotypically normal, immortal cell lines derived from the inner cell mass (ICM) of pre-implantation embryos (Martin, 1981; Evans and Kaufman, 1981).
evidence: Supported by citations to Martin, 1981 and Evans and Kaufman, 1981

claim: ESCs are pluripotent, able to differentiate into all future cell lineages of the embryo proper.
source: ESCs are pluripotent, able to differentiate into all future cell lineages of the embryo proper, and able to retain pluripotency through successive rounds of self-renewing cell division (Beddington and Robertson, 1989; Suemori et al., 1990; Lallemand and Brûlet, 1990; Martello and Smith, 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: ESCs are able to retain pluripotency through successive rounds of self-renewing cell division.
source: ESCs are pluripotent, able to differentiate into all future cell lineages of the embryo proper, and able to retain pluripotency through successive rounds of self-renewing cell division (Beddington and Robertson, 1989; Suemori et al., 1990; Lallemand and Brûlet, 1990; Martello and Smith, 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: In mouse, pluripotent stem cells can be derived from several stages of development and exhibit gene expression profiles matching these developmental stages.
source: In mouse, pluripotent stem cells can be derived from several stages of development and exhibit gene expression profiles matching these developmental stages (Morgani et al., 2017; Riveiro and Brickman, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Morgani et al., 2017 and Riveiro and Brickman, 2020

claim: When cultured in serum and the cytokine LIF, mESCs constitute a dynamically heterogeneous cell culture model that contains populations that are primed, but not committed, for both primitive endoderm (PrE) and Epiblast.
source: When cultured in serum and the cytokine LIF, they constitute a dynamically heterogeneous cell culture model that contains populations that are primed, but not committed, for both primitive endoderm (PrE) and Epiblast.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript text

claim: Primed ESC populations exhibit biases in differentiation but will readily interconvert when left in self-renewing culture.
source: These populations exhibit biases in differentiation but will readily interconvert when left in self-renewing culture (Canham et al., 2010; Morgani et al., 2013; Illingworth et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: NACL culture condition supports heterogeneous ESC culture and sustains effective propagation of pluripotency and high levels of germline transmission.
source: While these conditions involve serum, we recently defined a culture condition that supports heterogeneous ESC culture, and at the same time sustains effective propagation of pluripotency and high levels of germline transmission (Anderson et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Anderson et al., 2017

claim: NACL refers to culture condition with N2B27, Activin A, Chiron, and LIF.
source: We refer to this culture condition as NACL for N2B27, Activin A, Chiron, and LIF.
evidence: Direct definition provided in the text

claim: RACL media with RPMI base supports PrE differentiation and expansion.
source: A similar defined media with the same components but an RPMI base (RACL) supports PrE differentiation and expansion (Anderson et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Anderson et al., 2017

claim: Previous time lapse studies have explored the role of heterogeneity in ESCs and made comparisons between naïve culture in serum and media based on small molecule inhibitors of GSK3 and MEK, in addition to LIF (2i/LIF).
source: Several time lapse studies have explored the role of heterogeneity in ESCs, and comparisons have been made between naïve culture in serum and media based on small molecule inhibitors of GSK3 and mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK), in addition to LIF (2i/LIF) (Singer et al., 2014; Abranches et al., 2014; Filipczyk et al., 2015; Cannon et al., 2015; Hastreiter et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: Previous studies have focused on the dynamic heterogeneity of pluripotency factors which are associated with supporting the pluripotent state and Epiblast specification in vivo.
source: Taken together, these studies have focussed on the dynamic heterogeneity of pluripotency factors which are associated with supporting the pluripotent state and Epiblast specification in vivo.
evidence: Summary of previous research findings

claim: Previous studies have not assessed the expression of lineage-specific markers, how cells progress into differentiation and the role of priming in differentiation.
source: Although they have explored the role of pluripotency factors in lineage priming (Strebinger et al., 2019), they have not assessed the expression of lineage-specific markers, how cells progress into differentiation and the role of priming in differentiation.
evidence: Statement about gaps in previous research

claim: The segregation of PrE from Epiblast in vivo is regulated by the FGF/ERK pathway.
source: In vivo, the segregation of PrE from Epiblast is regulated by the FGF/ERK pathway (Chazaud et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chazaud et al., 2006

claim: The inhibition of the FGF/ERK pathway results in an expansion of Epiblast identity and loss of PrE, both in vivo and in vitro.
source: The inhibition of this pathway results in an expansion of Epiblast identity and loss of PrE, both in vivo and in vitro (Nichols et al., 2009; Yamanaka et al., 2010; Hamilton and Brickman, 2014; Saiz et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: Inhibition of MEK with PD03 is an important component of the defined ESC culture system known as 2i/LIF.
source: Based on the activity of this pathway in supporting PrE differentiation in vivo, inhibition of the kinase upstream ERK, MEK, with a pharmacological antagonist (PD03) is an important component of the defined ESC culture system known as 2i/LIF (Ying et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ying et al., 2008

claim: ERK activation is associated with cell cycle progression and is thought to stimulate G1/S transition.
source: Additionally, ERK activation is also associated with cell cycle progression and is thought to stimulate G1/S transition (Yamamoto et al., 2006; Ter Huurne et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yamamoto et al., 2006 and Ter Huurne et al., 2017

claim: G1 lengthening has been functionally related to endoderm differentiation.
source: Although G1 lengthening has been functionally related to endoderm differentiation (Calder et al., 2013; Pauklin and Vallier, 2013; Coronado et al., 2013), it is not clear how ERK stimulation of cell cycle progression relates to its capacity to induce differentiation.
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on samples from 2i/LIF and days 1, 2, 3, 4, and 7 of in vitro PrE differentiation using MARS-seq.
source: To assess lineage-specific transcriptional heterogeneity in PrE differentiation and compare the events occurring in vitro to those occurring in vivo, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing by MARS-seq (Jaitin et al., 2014) on samples from 2i/LIF and days 1, 2, 3, 4, and 7 of in vitro PrE differentiation (Figure 1A).
evidence: Experimental data described in text and shown in Figure 1A

claim: A Sox2-GFP and Hhex-mCherry double fluorescent reporter cell line was used to track both endodermal and Epiblast lineages.
source: To track both endodermal and Epiblast lineages, we used a Sox2-GFP and Hhex-mCherry double fluorescent reporter cell line (Figure 1A; Anderson et al., 2017).
evidence: Experimental method described in text with reference to Figure 1A and citation

claim: Nine clusters were detected using unsupervised clustering of the scRNA-seq data.
source: We detected nine clusters using unsupervised clustering (Figure 1B).
evidence: Analysis result shown in Figure 1B

claim: Clusters 1, 5, and 6 were composed of 2i/LIF cells.
source: Clusters 1, 5, and 6 were composed of 2i/LIF cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, Table 1).
evidence: Data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and Table 1

claim: Differentiating cells resolved into two branches: a PrE-like branch (clusters 3, 7, and 4) and an Epiblast-like branch (clusters 0 and 2).
source: Differentiating cells (from days 2 to 7) appeared to resolve into two branches: a PrE-like branch (clusters 3, 7, and 4) expressing progressively increasing levels of Hhex-mCherry (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and PrE markers such as Dab2, Gata6, Pdgfra, and Sox17 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A); and an Epiblast-like branch (clusters 0 and 2) with cells that appear to remain Epiblast-like, continuing to express pluripotency markers (Sox2-GFP, see Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Klf2, Nanog, Sox2, and Rex1, see Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Data analysis shown in multiple supplementary figures

claim: Distinct endodermal signatures were identified as early as day 2 of differentiation.
source: We identified distinct endodermal signatures as early as day 2 (Figure 1C), suggesting that some cells at day 2 were already primed towards endoderm differentiation.
evidence: Data shown in Figure 1C

claim: The endodermal genes found at day 2 of the PrE branch were not upregulated at day 2 in the NEDiff branch.
source: The endodermal genes found at day 2 of the PrE branch (PrE in Figure 1C) were not upregulated at day 2 in the NEDiff branch (NEDiff in Figure 1C), supporting the notion that the transcriptional signature for PrE appeared on day 2 in a subpopulation of these cultures.
evidence: Data comparison shown in Figure 1C

claim: Day 7 PrE cluster 4 was most similar to PrE from E4.5 embryos.
source: Our day 7 PrE cluster 4 was most similar to PrE from E4.5, the earlier emerging PrE cluster 7, first appearing at day 2, resembled PrE from E3.5, while the rest of the clusters were most similar to E3.5 Epiblast (Figure 1D).
evidence: Comparison analysis shown in Figure 1D using CAT tool

claim: The earlier emerging PrE cluster 7, first appearing at day 2, resembled PrE from E3.5 embryos.
source: Our day 7 PrE cluster 4 was most similar to PrE from E4.5, the earlier emerging PrE cluster 7, first appearing at day 2, resembled PrE from E3.5, while the rest of the clusters were most similar to E3.5 Epiblast (Figure 1D).
evidence: Comparison analysis shown in Figure 1D

claim: An early PrE-like cell type arises by day 2 in vitro.
source: Based on these comparisons, we believe that our in vitro model is a good tool for deconstructing transcriptional signatures of differentiation and that an early PrE-like cell type arises by day 2 in vitro.
evidence: Inference based on data comparisons

claim: Cells that differentiate into PrE are dividing faster at the beginning of the differentiation process (day 3).
source: Analysis of mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) division times and cell counts showed that cells that differentiate into PrE are dividing faster at the beginning of the differentiation process (day 3, left panel) and that selected survival likely takes place later in differentiation (days 4 and 5, right panel).
evidence: Time lapse analysis shown in Figure 2D

claim: Selected survival of PrE cells likely takes place later in differentiation (days 4 and 5).
source: Analysis of mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) division times and cell counts showed that cells that differentiate into PrE are dividing faster at the beginning of the differentiation process (day 3, left panel) and that selected survival likely takes place later in differentiation (days 4 and 5, right panel).
evidence: Time lapse analysis shown in Figure 2D

claim: Cell cycle length at day 3 shows a decrease in the PrE cells division time (13.00 ± 4 hr) compared to NEDiff cells (20.00 ± 6 hr).
source: We observed a decrease in the division time of the PrE cluster with cell division accelerating primarily on day 3 of differentiation (13.00 ± 4 hr for PrE and 20.00 ± 6 hr for NEDiff clusters on day 3) (Figure 2D, E, Table 2).
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Figure 2D, E and Table 2

claim: Culture conditions promoted endoderm specification by providing an environment that favoured the proliferation of a PrE-primed population.
source: This is the point in time when PrE clones became distinguishable from NEDiff cells in the time lapse video (Video 1) and suggested that culture conditions promoted endoderm specification by providing an environment that favoured the proliferation of a PrE-primed population.
evidence: Inference from time lapse data shown in Video 1

claim: NEDiff cells showed a higher rate of cell death and reduced survival compared to PrE cells.
source: We also observed a higher rate of cell death and reduced survival (Table 2) in the NEDiff cells, suggesting an additional level of selective cell survival in the PrE progenitor population.
evidence: Data shown in Table 2

claim: 12.6 ± 0.6% of the total population upregulated Hhex expression during the first 72 hr, transitioning into the PrE cluster.
source: We found that 12.6 ± 0.6% of the total population upregulated Hhex expression during the first 72 hr, thereby transitioning into the PrE cluster.
evidence: Quantitative analysis of time lapse data

claim: After the 72-hr time point, only 1.9 ± 1.2% of the cells were able to transit between clusters.
source: However, after the 72-hr time point, only 1.9 ± 1.2% of the cells were able to transit between clusters.
evidence: Quantitative analysis of time lapse data

claim: Competence to enter the endoderm lineage was lost after the first 3 days of the differentiation.
source: This suggested that competence to enter the endoderm lineage was lost after the first 3 days of the differentiation, indicating that proliferation was enhanced following lineage choice.
evidence: Inference from transition probability data

claim: Before commitment at day 3, 86% of prospective PrE cells survived to generate colonies of PrE, whereas only 61% of the NEDiff survived.
source: Before commitment took place at day 3, 86% of prospective PrE cells survived to generate colonies of PrE, whereas only 61% of the NEDiff survived (Table 2).
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Table 2

claim: After commitment at 72 hr, 92% of cells in the PrE cluster survived, whereas only 39% of the cells in the NEDiff cluster survived.
source: This difference in survival was further enhanced following commitment at 72 hr and continuing throughout differentiation: from this point onwards, 92% of cells in the PrE cluster survived, whereas only 39% of the cells in the NEDiff cluster did (Table 2).
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Table 2

claim: On day 3, the cell cycle contribution has a more significant impact on the population composition, while cell survival has an increasing dominant impact on days 4 and 5.
source: We found that on day 3, the cell cycle contribution has a more significant impact on the population composition, while cell survival has an increasing dominant impact on days 4 and 5.
evidence: Analysis of mathematical model predictions

claim: Differentiation was selecting for committed endoderm at two levels: proliferation first, and cell survival later.
source: Therefore, it appeared that differentiation was selecting for committed endoderm at two levels: proliferation first, and cell survival later.
evidence: Inference from mathematical modeling and experimental data

claim: Endodermal gene expression became more homogeneous and the level of endodermal transcription in individual cells increases from days 2 to 7.
source: Furthermore scRNA-seq suggested that the PrE population also accrued more endodermal identity as it expanded, such that endodermal gene expression not only became more homogeneous, but the level of endodermal transcription in individual cells increases from days 2 to 7 (Figure 1C), a process we refer to as progressive induction.
evidence: scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C

claim: Cells that will give rise to PrE (PrE Fate) show higher Hhex intensity at day 2 compared to cells that eventually would not differentiate (NEDiff Fate).
source: We found that there was a tendency for PrE progenitor cells (PrE Fate) to express Hhex at higher levels (0.18) compared to cells that are non-endodermal progenitors (NEDiff Fate, 0.15) (Figure 3B, Table 3).
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Figure 3B and Table 3

claim: Day 2 Hhex-high cells produced significantly more PDGFRA-positive PrE than either the Hhex-low or unsorted populations.
source: Consistent with the time lapse analysis, we observed that the day 2 Hhex-high cells produced significantly more PDGFRA-positive PrE than either the Hhex-low or unsorted populations (Figure 3C).
evidence: Experimental data from FACS sorting and differentiation assay shown in Figure 3C

claim: NACL culture supports a population of ESCs primed for PrE (Hhex-mCherry positive) and Epiblast (NANOG positive), within the OCT4-positive ESC population.
source: We confirmed our previous observations (Anderson et al., 2017) that NACL culture supports a population of ESCs primed for PrE (Hhex-mCherry positive) and Epiblast (NANOG positive), within the OCT4-positive ESC population (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A with citation

claim: In NACL culture, 86% of cells survived, and cells divided every 17 hr on average.
source: In NACL culture, we observed that 86% of cells survived, and cells divided every 17 hr on average.
evidence: Quantitative analysis of time lapse data

claim: The level of cell death was not significantly different between the three Hhex compartments in NACL culture (9% in the High, 12% in the Mid, and 21% in the Low).
source: The level of cell death was not significantly different between the three compartments in our dataset (9% in the High, 12% in the Mid, and 21% in the Low, Table 4), so we went on to examine transitions.
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Table 4

claim: In NACL, the Low Hhex cells exhibited significantly shorter division times (14.67 ± 5 hr) than the High Hhex cells (17.33 ± 6 hr).
source: Here, the Low Hhex cells exhibited significantly shorter division times than the High Hhex cells (14.67 ± 5 vs. 17.33 ± 6 hr, Figure 4F, Table 4).
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Figure 4F and Table 4

claim: Cells in PD03 expressed significantly lower levels of Hhex than in the NACL control.
source: Given the direct relation between ERK stimulation and Hhex upregulation (Hamilton and Brickman, 2014), we found unsurprisingly that cells in PD03 expressed significantly lower levels of Hhex than in the NACL control (Figure 5B).
evidence: Data shown in Figure 5B with citation

claim: PD03 treatment had little effect on cell survival (80% cells that survived vs. 86% in NACL).
source: At the level of cell survival, PD03 treatment had little effect (80% cells that survived vs. 86% in NACL, Table 4).
evidence: Quantitative data shown in Table 4

claim: Culture in PD03 produced significant alterations to both cell cycle length and cell state transitions.
source: However, culture in PD03 produced significant alterations to both cell cycle length (Figure 5D) and cell state transitions (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A

claim: Cell cycle length was correlated between sisters and cousins, but not mother–daughter in NACL.
source: In NACL, we found that cell cycle length was correlated between sisters and cousins, but not mother–daughter (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Correlation analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C

claim: Cell cycle correlation between sisters and cousins was reduced or eliminated in the presence of PD03.
source: However, we found that cell cycle correlation between sisters and cousins was reduced or eliminated in the presence of PD03 (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Correlation analysis shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2D

claim: Culture in NACL with PD17 resulted in the same loss of cousin and sister correlation as that in response to inhibition of MEK.
source: Figure 5F shows that culture in NACL with PD17 resulted in the same loss of cousin and sister correlation as that in response to inhibition of its downstream kinase MEK, further supporting the role for this pathway as a primary determinant of cell cycle synchronization.
evidence: Data shown in Figure 5F

claim: PD03 was both more effective at inducing Low Hhex populations and producing a general decrease in cell cycle length compared to PD17.
source: Furthermore, PD03 was both more effective at inducing Low Hhex populations and producing a general decrease in cell cycle length (Figure 5F, right; Table 4).
evidence: Comparative data shown in Figure 5F and Table 4

claim: Despite the reduced effect of PD17 in ESC heterogeneity, PD17 was at least as effective as PD03 in its capacity to block synchronization.
source: However, despite the reduced effect of PD17 in ESC heterogeneity (Figure 5F, right), PD17 was at least as effective as PD03 in its capacity to block synchronization (Figure 5F, left; Figure 5—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Comparative data shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2E

claim: PD03 addition significantly increases the ratio between G1 and division time, even though it does not significantly change the G1 length itself in FUCCI cells.
source: PD03 addition significantly increases the ratio between G1 and division time (*p value <0.05, Kruskal–Wallis test), even though it does not significantly change the G1 length itself in FUCCI cells.
evidence: Data shown in Figure 6A with statistical test

claim: Cells cultured in 2i/LIF for two passages show a faster cell cycle than when PD03 was added for a short period.
source: Cells cultured in 2i/LIF for two passages show a faster cell cycle than when PD03 was added for a short period (**p value <0.01, ****p value <0.0001, Kruskal–Wallis test).
evidence: Data shown in Figure 6A with statistical test

claim: PrE differentiated cells show a longer G1 phase and an increase in G1 ratio as they proceed along the differentiation process.
source: Primitive Endoderm (PrE) differentiated cells show a longer G1 phase and an increase in G1 ratio as they proceed along the differentiation process.
evidence: Data shown in Figure 6B

claim: Division time is faster at day 3 and then it slows down during PrE differentiation, consistent with the previous dataset.
source: Division time is faster at day 3 and then it slows down, consistent with the previous dataset. *p value <0.05, **p value <0.01, ***p value <0.001, ****p value <0.0001, Kruskal–Wallis test.
evidence: Data shown in Figure 6B with statistical tests

claim: There is an increase in cells expressing G1 transcripts as they progress through the endoderm lineage in vitro.
source: As shown in Figure 6C, we observed the same trend of cells entering G1 as they progress through the endoderm lineage.
evidence: scRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 6C

claim: There is an increase in cells expressing G1 transcripts as they progress into the endodermal lineage in vivo.
source: We found an increase in cells expressing G1 transcripts as they progressed into the endodermal lineage in vivo.
evidence: Analysis of published in vivo dataset

claim: Around the time of implantation E4.5, there was a robust difference in cell cycle phase between Epiblast, which was mostly in S phase, and PrE, where almost half of the cells were in G1.
source: Around the time of implantation E4.5, there was a robust difference in cell cycle phase between Epiblast, which was mostly in S phase, and PrE, where almost half of the cells were in G1.
evidence: Analysis of published in vivo dataset

claim: In ESC self-renewal in vitro, naïve Epiblast-like cells proliferate faster than those primed for PrE differentiation.
source: In ESC self-renewal in vitro, naïve Epiblast-like cells proliferate faster than those primed for PrE differentiation, but when the base media is changed, the tides are turned, and the PrE-primed population develops the proliferative advantage.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings

claim: When the base media is changed, the PrE-primed population develops the proliferative advantage.
source: In ESC self-renewal in vitro, naïve Epiblast-like cells proliferate faster than those primed for PrE differentiation, but when the base media is changed, the tides are turned, and the PrE-primed population develops the proliferative advantage.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings

claim: Differential culture conditions identify the appropriate lineage-biased populations and stimulate their relative expansion.
source: This suggests that differential culture conditions identify the appropriate lineage-biased populations and stimulate their relative expansion.
evidence: Inference from experimental observations

claim: The differentiation process is both selective and progressively inductive.
source: The differentiation process we define is both selective and progressively inductive.
evidence: Summary interpretation of experimental findings

claim: By day 3 in differentiation, all the future founder cells in the culture are set, and further commitment does not occur.
source: By day 3 in differentiation, all the future founder cells in the culture are set, and further commitment does not occur.
evidence: Inference from time lapse and transition probability data

claim: An increase in G1 would give cycling cells more time to respond to inductive signals, ultimately leading to increased responsiveness to differentiation cues.
source: An increase in G1 would give cycling cells more time to respond to inductive signals, ultimately leading to increased responsiveness to differentiation cues.
evidence: Mechanistic interpretation of experimental findings

claim: The link between G1 phase and commitment of pluripotent stem cells into differentiation was first described in 1987 in embryonal carcinoma cells.
source: While the link between G1 phase and commitment of pluripotent stem cells into differentiation was first described in 1987 in embryonal carcinoma cells (Mummery et al., 1987), the recent development of the cell cycle reporter cell line FUCCI has allowed for more detailed findings in this field.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mummery et al., 1987

claim: The G1 fraction of ESCs has an enhanced capacity to respond to endoderm differentiation signals both in mouse and human.
source: It has been functionally demonstrated that the G1 fraction of ESCs has an enhanced capacity to respond to endoderm differentiation signals both in mouse (Coronado et al., 2013) and human (Calder et al., 2013; Pauklin and Vallier, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: G1 phase lengthening accompanies differentiation in neural, pancreatic, and intestinal cell lineages.
source: The notion that G1 phase lengthening accompanies differentiation has been shown in other cell lineages such as neural (Lange et al., 2009; Roccio et al., 2013), pancreatic (Kim et al., 2015; Krentz et al., 2017), and intestinal (Carroll et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: Mammalian cells share the striking quality of being synchronized in cell cycle length between members of the same generation (sisters and cousins), but not with the previous generation (mother–daughter).
source: Mammalian cells share the striking quality of being synchronized in cell cycle length between members of the same generation (sisters and cousins), but not with the previous generation (mother–daughter). This was originally demonstrated in both a lymphoblast cell line and ESCs (Sandler et al., 2015; Waisman et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sandler et al., 2015 and Waisman et al., 2019

claim: The determinant of cell cycle synchronization is a factor located within the ERK pathway downstream of MEK.
source: Our observations suggest that this determinant is a factor located within the ERK pathway downstream of MEK, as culture with either the MEK inhibitor PD03 and/or the FGFR antagonist PD17 eliminates these correlations.
evidence: Inference from experimental data with PD03 and PD17

claim: FGF/ERK regulation is likely a key nexus for cell cycle synchronization activity.
source: Thus FGF/ERK regulation is likely a key nexus for this activity, and our observations suggest this activity is independent of its role in regulating differentiation.
evidence: Inference from experimental observations

claim: The scRNA-seq data have been deposited in the Gene Expression Omnibus under accession number GSE200534.
source: The scRNA-seq data used in this study have been deposited in the Gene Expression Omnibus, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/, the accession number is GSE200534.
evidence: Data availability statement
